solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ill-disposed collie had some ringed spots of colour

indicators.note: badly disposed reads as badly arranged, so the dog's letters are set out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written: the sheepdog

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered sheepdog with a coat marked by ringed patches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-disposed' looks like the dog's mood but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocelli are eye-like markings, such as those on a peacock's tail feathers or butterfly wings.

clue.text: Old carriage driver, teacher travelling round South American city

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the word's letters move into a new order
round means surrounding, so the city sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
Rio de Janeiro in Brazil

explanation.surface: A teacher touring a South American city.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome and Greece the person who drove a racing or war chariot was called this.

clue.text: The french female in command is secular

blocks.note: la is the feminine form of the in French
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman in charge is not religious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The french female' reads as a woman from France, but means the French feminine article.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means relating to the laity rather than the clergy, hence non-religious.

blocks.note: straight reading: a pointless observation
setter's reading: a remark on being without work, since out-of-work people are said to be idle

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the adjective meaning pointless also means out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle remark is a casual, purposeless comment, and idle also means not working.

blocks.note: to be anti something is to oppose it
a plain synonym

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: being opposed to war.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiwar describes opposition to fighting between nations, such as a peace protest.

blocks.note: first meaning: Alban, the Austrian twentieth-century composer of Wozzeck
second meaning: a short word for an iceberg, most of which lies hidden in the main, the sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' looks like 'mostly', and it means that too, but the main is also the sea, where the bulk of an iceberg sits out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg wrote atonal operas, and berg is short for an iceberg, whose bulk lies underwater.

blocks.note: surface reading: an ornamental bloom made of ceramic
setter's reading: porcelain is another name for fine crockery, and that word starts the name of a real garden plant

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a decorative ornament; it is a living garden plant whose first word is the crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: The china aster is an annual garden plant from East Asia with large daisy-like blooms.

clue.text: One who revises stories removing first and last bits democratically initially within

indicators.note: says to drop the opening and closing letters of the word before it
revising reworks something, so the letters are rearranged; the word also serves the definition
initially keeps only the opening letter of the word before it
within places one letter inside the rearranged group

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of democratically

explanation.surface: A newspaper sub trims the ends of articles in a democratic spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the S at each end of stories, rearrange the five letters left, and put D inside. 'Revises' does double duty, as definition and anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor checks and corrects texts before publication, which is exactly revising them.

clue.text: Fool to start digging beneath cape.

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first of the following word is kept

blocks.note: opening letter of digging
a plain synonym
a cape is a headland, as in Beachy Head

explanation.surface: An instruction that the idiot should begin digging below the cape.
explanation.walkthrough: Headlands are often called heads, so cape gives HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunderhead is a stupid person, an old-fashioned insult equivalent to blockhead or dolt.

indicators.note: something relaid is put down again in a different way, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A connecting stretch of railway line is being laid down again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linking' looks like an adjective for a railway spur, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracketing things together groups or associates them, so it means connecting or putting them in the same class.

clue.text: Young toad initially found in pond!

definitions.text: Young toad initially found in pond!

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: young things are new
first letter of toad

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly spots what they think is a baby toad in the pond.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a loose description: a small amphibian easily mistaken for a young toad, found in ponds.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small amphibian with a tail that breeds in ponds alongside frogs and toads.

indicators.note: being included by something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: BR is a standard abbreviation for brown
two O shapes look like a pair of eggs

explanation.surface: A yob scrambles brown eggs into his breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: O for egg is a crossword staple from its shape; two of them are eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A boor is a coarse, ill-mannered person, much the same as a lout or oaf.

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep
rustling is raiding farms to steal livestock

explanation.surface: Stealing sheep is a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Ram-raiding is driving a vehicle through a shop front to loot it; the clue puns it as raiding for rams.
explanation.definitionFit: Ram-raiding is a form of burglary in which a car is smashed through a shop window.

blocks.note: first meaning: an apparatus that drives off moisture
second meaning, playful: whatever causes vanishing

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: to evaporate can also mean to vanish, so a magician might be called one.
explanation.definitionFit: The device removes water as vapour, and evaporate also means to vanish into thin air.

indicators.note: to become is to turn into something else, so these letters turn into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man was trained to be watchful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like part of 'to become' but belongs to the anagram letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the alert is to be watchful and ready for danger, the same as vigilant.

clue.text: Blot out well read former pupil taking the lead

indicators.note: taking the lead means going in front, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil of a school
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: An educated ex-pupil leads the way in erasing something.
explanation.walkthrough: Old boy is the British term for a former pupil of a particular school.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out or erase completely, as a blot of ink obscures writing.

blocks.note: underdone meat is still red inside
steak is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: A diner ordering a steak cooked rare.
explanation.walkthrough: Rare suggests scarcity, but here it is the cooking sense; the whole clue also describes the answer, beef being the classic example.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef and lamb are classed as red meat, and a rare steak is visibly red inside.

clue.text: Allowed to return during visit at this home

definitions.note: an adjective: the clue means the kind of home called a stately home

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
during places one thing in the middle of another, so it sits inside

blocks.note: to be let do something is to be allowed
a stay is a visit

explanation.surface: A guest is permitted to come back during a visit to this house.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the set phrase stately home, a grand country house open to visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Stately describes the grand aristocratic country houses of Britain, called stately homes.

clue.text: Right to be leaving unfortunate dire trip in turbulent water

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter is taken out
something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor is right to quit a dreadful voyage through rough seas.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one R from the eight letters of 'dire trip', then rearrange the remaining seven.
explanation.definitionFit: A riptide is a strong current where opposing flows meet, making the sea rough and dangerous.

clue.text: A beef drink prepared and used in the kitchen

definitions.note: a description of the thing, a kitchen utensil

indicators.note: a prepared dish is made up from its ingredients, so these letters are worked into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Making a beef tea, a Bovril-like drink, in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen setting makes the drink feel like the answer; the letters of the first three words make a utensil instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated blade for slicing loaves is a standard kitchen tool.

clue.text: Claptrap from Greek character getting up from bed on board first

indicators.note: in a down answer getting up means rising, so the letters are read bottom to top
first says that piece goes at the front of the answer

blocks.note: a bunk is a bed on a ship
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Nonsense from a Greek who has just risen from a ship's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunkum is nonsense or empty talk, the same as claptrap or humbug.

indicators.note: before says the first piece is placed ahead of the second

blocks.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
a standard short form of the weekday

explanation.surface: A woman watched a rugby match ahead of Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a woman's name, from the Old Testament heroine, so it fits a lady.

indicators.note: going back means reading the word in the opposite direction

blocks.note: past tense of run
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: Someone dashed home with a Dutch skin cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Nard, or spikenard, is an aromatic balm made in ancient times from a Himalayan plant.

definitions.note: names a place: a town in Cambridgeshire

blocks.note: a plain synonym
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A small harbour somewhere in the Cambridgeshire Fens.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridgeshire is a county in eastern England; the town lies near Ely in the Fens.
explanation.definitionFit: Littleport is a small Fenland town north of Ely, in the county of Cambridgeshire.

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: the word that goes before speaker in the name of a sound device
second meaning: easily heard

explanation.surface: A talker whose voice carries a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This speaker' is a loose pointer to a loudspeaker, whose first word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with great volume of sound is easy to hear from far off.

blocks.note: P is an abbreviation for priest
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A strait-laced cleric arriving at the brink.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim means stiffly proper and easily shocked by impropriety, much like prudish.

definitions.note: names a thing found in rugby: a high kick

blocks.note: time is up when it is finished
a plain synonym
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A team is done for and has dropped down the table in rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is a football code played with an oval ball; this is a tactic in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The up-and-under is a high, hanging kick that lets chasing players reach the catcher as the ball comes down.

blocks.note: first meaning, a verb: to tone down or soften
second meaning, a noun: a fit of anger

explanation.surface: A plea to calm down an irritable spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to soften it, and to be in a temper is to be angry.
